the metric fluctuations induced by quantum matter fields in an evaporat-ing black hole background geometry grow to macroscopically important levels well before the Plan-ckian regime is entered, but that there are important corrections to the simple correlation between fluctuations of the energy-momentum tensor near the horizon and far away from it, which had been assumed in earlier work.

the stochastic gravity formalisms is a promising tool for the study of quantum fluctuations of an evaporating black holes, and that the assumption of a direct relation between the fluctuations of energy fluxes far from and near the horizon is not correct, and needs to be replaced by an appropriate generalization.

we have not yet been able to prove the existence or absence of a black hole singularity.
we do not understand how to make sense of the Hawking evaporation process in a quantum theory of gravity.

the stochastic gravity approach, when applied to the spherically symmetric sector of metric perturbation fluctuations in an evaporating geometry, is a useful tool for probing the quantum nature of spacetime, but only after a careful analysis of the physical meaning of the results and the limitations of the approach is carried out.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the back-reaction of the Hawking radiation on the black hole spacetime geometry is a non-perturbative quantum effect that is not captured by the stochastic gravity formalisms.

, in the case of evaporating black holes, quantum gravity effects are expected to manifest themselves as a stochastic background of metric perturbances, and the horizon of the black hole is not a well defined object.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the stochastic gravity formalisms, which have been developed in the context of quantum field theory on curved spacetime, can be used to study quantum gravitational effects on the spacetime geometry.

the spacetime fluctuations around an evaporating Schwarzschild black hole background are not negligible, but rather become important at a time scale which is much longer than the Planck time, yet still much shorter than the evaporation time.
